summary.short: Omnibus French act adapting law to EU rules in economic, energy, transport and other fields. Its data-centre provisions (Art. 25, Code de l'énergie Art. L. 236-1 to L. 236-3) require energy-data reporting for sites of 500 kW or more, waste-heat recovery at 1 MW or more, and allow administrative fines up to 50,000 euros per data centre.
summary.long: Law n° 2025-391 of 30 April 2025 (JORF 2 May 2025) is an omnibus act adapting French law to EU rules across economic, financial, environmental, energy, transport and health fields. Article 25 adds a data-centre chapter to the Energy Code (Art. L. 236-1 to L. 236-3) that applies to all data centres, with defence-related centres excluded from the reporting duty. Centres with installed capacity of 500 kW or more must transmit administrative, environmental and energy information on an EU digital platform and make related data public. Centres of 1 MW or more must recover their waste heat, subject to decree-defined derogations. Projects of 1 MW or more require a cost-benefit analysis of energy efficiency (Art. L. 233-5). The administrative authority may issue a formal notice with a deadline of at most one year and, if it is not followed, an administrative fine of up to 50,000 euros per data centre; it may publish the sanction for two months to five years. Ministers set general rules on siting, grid availability and cooling water. Article 25 I to III enter into force on 1 October 2025, and Art. L. 236-1 from the day after publication. Other titles cover investment-service inducements, electricity aggregation, class actions and energy-efficiency duties for companies and public bodies.

notes: Part 1 of 2 (Titres I and II, Articles 1 to 26). Relations and notes cover only this part. Data-centre provisions in this part are Art. 25 II 9° (Code de l'énergie, L. 233-5 cost-benefit analysis; L. 236-1 to L. 236-3 data centres with thresholds of 500 kW and 1 MW). Art. 25 VI makes L. 236-1 enter into force the day after publication via a reference to 'le 3° du II du présent article', but L. 236-1 is inserted by II 9°, not II 3°; as written the cross-reference does not match. Ordinance authorisations (Art. 1 II, 2 III, 2 VII, 25 V) are not transpositions by this text. Many amendments are table updates to codified lists of ordinance and law provisions. Part 2 of 2 (Arts 27-41). Relations stated in this part only; amending articles are merged into one row per target code, citing the first article. target_instrument_id is an empty string where the target is not in the registry (the schema requires a string). The text refers to a 'règlement MACF' (Art. 33 I) without naming it in this part; the link to Regulation (EU) 2023/956 rests on Art. 33 II and Art. 34. Art. 36 I contains 'İ.-' where 'I.-' is presumably meant. Art. 40 cites EU directives but does not use transposition wording, so these are recorded as cross_references. The Nota refers to a rectificatif (JO n° 109, 10 May 2025) that is not reflected here. Art. 39 quotes omit the HTML-entity guillemets used in the source. Relations stated only in other instruments (e.g., the repeal of Regulation 1005/2009 in the title quoted in Art. 35 2° b) are not recorded.
